6 Sovereign AI Red Lines for NHS England

Patient Safety & Clinical Autonomy

  • AI must augment, not replace, human clinical judgment in critical care decisions.
  • Compliance with Medical Devices Regulations 2002 and patient safety frameworks.
  • Algorithms must be transparent and auditable, adhering to the NHS AI Lab's guidance on explainable AI.

Data Privacy & Confidentiality

  • Strict adherence to GDPR, Data Protection Act 2018, and NHS Digital's data sharing agreements.
  • No re-identification of anonymized patient data without explicit, informed consent.
  • Secure data handling protocols aligned with ISO 27001 and NCSC guidelines.

Bias & Equity

  • Rigorous testing and mitigation of algorithmic bias to ensure equitable outcomes across all demographic groups.
  • Adherence to ethical guidelines from the Centre for Data Ethics and Innovation (CDEI).
  • Avoidance of exacerbating existing health inequalities through AI deployment.

Accountability & Oversight

  • Clear lines of accountability for AI system performance and outcomes, as per the AI Act.
  • Independent ethical review and oversight for all high-risk AI applications in healthcare.
  • Integration with existing NHS governance structures and regulatory bodies like the CQC.

Cybersecurity & Resilience

  • AI systems must be resilient to cyberattacks and operate securely within the NHS N3/HSCN network.
  • Compliance with the Network and Information Systems Regulations 2018.
  • Proactive threat intelligence integration and continuous security monitoring.

Public Trust & Transparency

  • Open communication with the public about AI use cases, benefits, and limitations in healthcare.
  • Clear mechanisms for patient feedback and redressal regarding AI decisions.
  • Engagement with patient advocacy groups and civil society for continuous improvement.
